title: October New-Vehicle Sales Set for a Modest Rise as Forecasters Flag Costly Loans and a Slow EV Recovery
dek: Cox Automotive and J.D. Power forecast October U.S. sales near a steady pace, while Q3 EV share recovered to 6.4% and monthly payments hit an October record.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Electric car charging points on a street, illustrating the U.S. and UK EV charging market

keyPoints: Cox Automotive expects October new-vehicle sales of about 1.38 million units, up 7.2% from a year earlier, with a seasonally adjusted pace near 16.1 million.
J.D. Power and GlobalData project 1,327,100 total sales, up 0.2% year over year, but a seasonally adjusted pace of 15.6 million and a 1.4% drop in retail sales after selling-day adjustment.
Kelley Blue Book data put U.S. Q3 EV sales at 262,649, or 6.4% of new-vehicle sales, down 39.5% from Q3 2025 but up from 5.8% in Q2.
J.D. Power expects the average monthly payment to reach a record $823 for an October, with interest rates at 6.81%.
body:
October is shaping up as a steady month for U.S. car sales, but the forecasts differ on how steady, and the financing picture is getting harder for buyers.

## Two forecasts, two readings

Cox Automotive, in a forecast released October 27, expects October new-vehicle sales to rise about 7.2% from last year to roughly 1.38 million units. Its seasonally adjusted annual rate, or SAAR, is near 16.1 million, up from 16 million in September and 15.7 million a year earlier. Cox says October has 28 selling days, three more than September, which flatters the raw comparison.

J.D. Power and GlobalData, in a forecast dated October 22, are more cautious. They project 1,327,100 total sales, up 0.2% year over year, and a SAAR of 15.6 million, flat from 2025. Their retail forecast is weaker: 1,109,500 units, down 1.4% on a selling-day-adjusted basis, although up 2.3% without that adjustment.

The gap is mostly about how each firm handles the selling-day calendar and a fleet-heavy mix. Neither forecast is an actual result. Monthly sales reports from automakers have not yet been published in the sources used for this story.

## Affordability is the constraint

J.D. Power's forecast is blunt about the cost of buying. It projects an average transaction price of $46,329, slightly lower, but average monthly payments rising 2.6% to $823, the highest October figure it has recorded. The average interest rate is projected at 6.81%, the highest October level since 2023, and lower trade-in equity is adding to the amount buyers finance.

Cox's economist Jonathan Gregory described the market as following a low-to-mid 16 million pace since March, supported by fleet sales, wealthier buyers and easier access to credit.

## EVs are recovering, but from a low base

Kelley Blue Book's Q3 estimates, reported October 12, show 262,649 EV sales in the United States, up 6.1% from Q2 but down 39.5% from a record Q3 2025 when buyers rushed ahead of expiring federal incentives. EVs made up about 6.4% of new-vehicle sales, the strongest share since Q3 2025.

Tesla still accounts for more than half of U.S. EV sales, though its volume fell about 20% year over year. Toyota and Lexus EV sales rose nearly fivefold, and Rivian posted 46% growth. Cox's Stephanie Valdez Streaty said the reset phase is largely behind the market, while high gasoline prices are also pushing some buyers toward electrified vehicles.

J.D. Power expects hybrids to reach 18.6% of retail sales in October, up 4 points, which suggests much of the demand shift is going to hybrids rather than battery-electric models.

## What to watch

Automaker October reports will show whether the forecasts were closer to the SAAR of 15.6 million or 16.1 million. Watch for the EV incentive picture as well: J.D. Power expects average EV incentives to fall 42% to $7,531 per unit from last October's elevated base.

This is an analysis of forecasts and Q3 estimates, not reported October results.

marketImpact.summary: A steady sales pace helps automakers with fleet and mainstream trucks, but the record monthly payment and higher rates pressure affordability. Hybrid demand gaining share is a mixed signal for battery-EV-focused names, while Toyota's EV and hybrid momentum stands out.
